segments.text: Hello guys welcome back to my youtube channel Safety Management Study
Guys today's topic is Safety Officer interview questions for industrial radiography
In this video we will learn what are the questions related to industrial radiography
which can be asked by a safety officer
So let's start this informative video
If you find the video informative then like the video and subscribe to the channel
The first question is what is an industrial radiography test?
What is a radiography test?
An industrial radiography test is a non-destructive test of pipes to ensure the quality and durability of a metal
We call a radiography test a non-destructive test
These tests are used to ensure the quality and durability of a metal pipe
Is there any defect in a metal pipe from a radiography test such as cracks, porosity, pinch holes or not?
Without any pipe being cut or damaged a metal pipe can be taken from an RT camera
A RT camera or a Gamma camera or an X-ray camera can be used
Generally after a pipe is old or welding a radiography test is done
Next, what is unit of measuring radiation?
We measure radiation in curie, microcevert or milli-rump
Next, what is a Geiger or a survey meter?
A Geiger or a survey meter is a device with which we measure radiation
or you can call it a safe distance
Next, what is a dosimeter?
A dosimeter is a device with which a radiographer who is taking in radiation
Next, how much radiation or dose of radiation is safe for a radiographer in one year?
Can a radiographer safely bear the amount of radiation in one year?
Its answer is 20 milli-ceverts per year
Next, what are the hazards of RT?
The link to all the questions is in the description box, you can check
There are hazards for radiography tests
Exposure to radiation for a long period of time
If you are exposed to radiation for a long period of time
then this is a hazard
Long term exposure
Loss of hair, cancer and high amount of radiation exposure
can cause skin burn and fatality
Next, unauthorized entry
Uncertified radiographers
Next, what are the safety precautions for RT?
Before radiography test, as a safety officer, you have to ensure all these safety points
Valid work permit, JSA or risk assessment
Valid license of the radioactive source
Calibration certificate of survey and dosimeter
Third party qualification certificate of radiographer
Third party certification, NRPB
means National Radiation Protection Board
should be approved
Medical or vision test report
Decay chart
Transport vehicle certificate
The vehicle from which RT equipment is being transported
should be approved by the Federal Authority for Nuclear Regulations
Adequate area proper barricade, warning sign and warning lights should be installed
Next, what is decay chart?
Decay chart is a chart
which shows the changes in the period of time in radioactivity
Next, what is controlled area?
Controlled area is such an area where radiographers can work
Next, how much radiation is safe for a radiographer?
7.5 micro-sever per hour
Safe limit for a radiographer
Next, what is the safe limit of radiation for?
General public
For general public, for 8 hours, 2.5 micro-sever per hour is safe
Next, what is film badge?
Film badge is a device which measures the time of radiographer RT
How many dose of radiation is being exposed in a month is measured
Next, what is isotope?
Isotopes are atoms whose atomic numbers are the same
but mass numbers are different
Isotopes can be stable or unstable
Isotopes are hazardous
because uncontrolled energy is released in the form of radiation wave
which damages living tissues and causes cancer
All questions are linked in the description box
You can also read the question answer
Thanks for watching
Be safe, be happy
